account:
Today has been mostly scheduled mayoral business, with two matters standing out. My morning grain inspection at the east-bank mill was incomplete: I could not find the miller or obtain stock records. I filed an honest report with the secretary. She also found no miller there this afternoon, and is checking appointments for a possible ten hundred follow-up tomorrow. That meeting is not confirmed, and I have no basis to conclude there is a grain shortage or wrongdoing.

An eighteen hundred hall lighting inspection has been added to the day's business. The baker said freight had told him about it, and the secretary and I have confirmed it. The baker also reports delivering eighty contracted loaves to the hall; I have not personally verified the delivery. That quantity and the lighting visit suggest preparations for some hall activity, but I do not know its purpose or who arranged it. I have asked for existing lighting plans or fault reports and someone responsible for maintenance, and proposed checking entrances, aisles, and the four tables before deciding on work.

The secretary has been safeguarding the appointment and supporting books and my mill report. She has just taken several written books from the appointments chest, apparently preparing for our business, though I have not read them now. No new council business has reached her. My neighbour hosted tea at the dockside cottage and offered to accompany the lighting visit; they are now waiting nearby, and the baker has arrived near the office. An earlier rumour about bridge or port changes remains unconfirmed: the written brief said no actual proposal had reached the secretary. I should not treat that rumour, or any guessed connection between these events, as fact.
